# waveform-playlist

> Multitrack Web Audio editor and player with canvas waveform visualization. Two UI surfaces over a shared framework-agnostic engine: a React component library (`@waveform-playlist/browser`, Tone.js backend) and framework-agnostic Web Components (`@dawcore/components`, native Web Audio backend).

## What It Does

waveform-playlist builds browser-based audio editing applications. Use the React surface (`@waveform-playlist/browser`) or the framework-agnostic Web Components surface (`@dawcore/components`, `<daw-editor>` — works in any framework or vanilla HTML). Both provide:

- Multitrack audio playback, mixing, and editing
- Canvas-based waveform and spectrogram rendering with zoom
- Click-to-seek, drag-to-select, clip drag/trim/split
- Vertical track reordering via drag grip or move up/down buttons (undoable)
- 20 real-time audio effects (reverb, delay, EQ, compression, etc.) via Tone.js
- Time-synchronized annotations with drag editing
- Recording with live waveform preview and VU level metering (input and output)
- WAV export with offline rendering
- BBC audiowaveform support for instant rendering of large files
- Sample rate hint for pre-computed peaks matching (`sampleRate` prop on provider)
- Theming via styled-components

## Packages

- `@waveform-playlist/browser` — Main package: React components, hooks, effects. `WaveformPlaylistProvider` takes an `arrangement` (an engine `Arrangement`, made with `useCreateArrangement(() => [audioTrack({ src })])`): the arrangement owns the tracks, the mix, the undo history and audio loading, and the provider derives what it publishes from it (no `tracks` / `onTracksChange` props). Playout engines (`@waveform-playlist/playout` + `tone`, or `@waveform-playlist/media-element-playout`) are optional peer dependencies; provide `createAdapter`/`createPlayout` to inject a custom engine.
- WAM 2.0 plugin hosting (from `@waveform-playlist/browser/tone`) — `addWamEffect`/`addWamEffectToTrack` host third-party [Web Audio Modules](https://www.webaudiomodules.com/) plugins alongside built-in Tone.js effects, requires native AudioContext mode (`configureGlobalContext({ nativeAudioContext: true })` from `@waveform-playlist/playout`; Firefox falls back automatically). `WamEffectGui` mounts plugin GUIs; `fetchWamLibrary`/`fetchWamDescriptor` from the optional `@dawcore/wam` peer discover community plugins. Same native-context call enables WAM hosting on `<daw-editor>`'s Tone.js backend (`createToneAdapter()`).
- `@waveform-playlist/core` — Data model: ClipTrack, AudioClip, sample-based math, track kinds (`ClipTrack.kind: 'audio' | 'midi'` is required and a track holds clips of that kind only; `createTrack({ kind })`, `assertTrackKind`, `splitTrackByKind` for older data; the engine and the arrangement throw on a mixed track, at the call that offered it: from a `useCreateArrangement` initializer that is a render error for an error boundary, from `arrangement.addTrack()` the caller's exception; the provider's `onError` is not called), `createSourceLoader` (key-based loader: `SourceState`, `SourceLoader`; read it with `useSyncExternalStore`), `audioTrack(options)` (a `ArrangementTrack` whose one clip names its audio by `src` (`ClipSource`: URL string, `Blob` or `File`; the clip is then a `LoadingClip`), `audioBuffer` or `waveformData`; `AudioTrackOptions`), `isLoadingClip`, and `AudioClip.src` (the source a clip came from). An arrangement (`createArrangement()` of `@waveform-playlist/engine`, or `useCreateArrangement` in React) holds and loads loading clips; `WaveformPlaylistProvider` draws a clip still loading as a placeholder when it has a `duration` or `waveformData`. Also in core: `carveClipRange` (punch-in), `enumerateMicrophones`/`watchMicrophoneDevices` (permission-free device listing), `createPanStage`/`panMatrix` (the gain-matrix track pan stage every renderer uses instead of a `StereoPannerNode` or Tone `Panner` — the pan law is the track's own (`PanLaw`: `'auto' | 'mono' | 'stereo'`; `trackPanLaw(track)` resolves it, `ClipTrack.panLaw` and `audioTrack({ panLaw })` are what a track enters with; in an arrangement the first decoded audio a track holds decides it and the clips never change it afterwards), so a stereo effect on a mono track neither changes its level nor collapses to mono), the effect registry shared by `<daw-editor>` and the React effects hooks (`registerEffect(type, definition)`, `unregisterEffect`, `getEffectDefinitions`, `prepareEffect`, `ensureEffectPrepared`, `needsPrepare`, `createEffectInstance(type, audioContext, params)`; types `NativeEffectDefinition`, `NativeEffectInstance`, `EffectParamDef`, `CreatedNativeEffect` — one `registerEffect()` call makes a custom AudioWorklet or native-node effect available to both surfaces; the registry state lives on `globalThis`, so two installed copies of core share it), `createMixerGesture()` (type `MixerGesture`: the gesture id of one mixer control, `{ gesture: gesture.id }` to the engine's mixer setters, so a slider drag is one undo step), the annotation store (`createAnnotationStore(initial?, { beforeChange? })`, types `AnnotationStore`, `AnnotationStoreOptions`: the one owner of the annotations both React providers take as `annotationStore`; React apps make it with `useCreateAnnotationStore` from `@waveform-playlist/browser`) and `applyAnnotationBounds(current, changes)` (writes `start`/`end` by id, keeps everything else, returns `current` when nothing changes)
- `@waveform-playlist/engine` — Framework-agnostic timeline engine: PlaylistEngine class, the arrangement, pure clip/timeline operations, event emitter. The arrangement (`createArrangement({ tracks?, undoLimit?, loadSource? })`, type `Arrangement`: `getTracks()`, `getMixer()`, `subscribe(listener)`, `sources`, `retry(src)`, and the track, clip, mixer and undo methods) owns the tracks, the mix (volume/mute/solo/pan/pan law by track id) and the undo history; `new PlaylistEngine({ adapter, arrangement })` plays it and makes its own when `arrangement` is left out, and an arrangement outlives its engine (one engine at a time; an engine with another `ppqn` converts the clips' ticks when it takes over, a different tempo is not converted). The engine owns selection, loop, zoom, master volume and selectedTrackId. `getState().tracks` is `readonly ClipTrack[]`, shared with the undo history and not a copy (frozen in development): copy a track before changing it and pass the copy to `updateTrack`. A track's own volume/muted/soloed/pan/panLaw fields seed its mix when its id has no mix entry yet (`setTracks` keeps the mix only of an id that is in the tracks it replaces); afterwards use `setTrackVolume`/`setTrackMute`/`setTrackSolo`/`setTrackPan`/`setTrackPanLaw`, which act on a track in the current tracks. Mixer moves are undo steps: each call is one by default, `{ gesture: id }` makes calls with one id one step (a fader drag; `createMixerGesture()` from `@waveform-playlist/core` makes the id per control and `attach(input)` ends it on the input's `change`, a held key's `keyup` or `blur`), `{ undoable: false }` is no step (written into every saved state; for automation); undo, redo and an aborted transaction bring back the mix of the state they return to. `setTrackRecording(trackId, recording)` (arrangement and engine; `recordingTrackIds`) marks the track a take is recording onto: it plays muted for the take, its stored mute in `getMixer()` is untouched, and it is not an undo step (not a record-arm). `updateTrack` may give a track a new id: it keeps its mix. Duplicate track ids, and duplicate clip ids within a track, throw. The arrangement also loads audio: its tracks are `ArrangementTrack`, whose clips are `AudioClip` or `LoadingClip` (a `src` and times in seconds; narrow with `isLoadingClip` before reading sample fields; a loading clip cannot be moved, trimmed or split, and one on a `kind: 'midi'` track throws). It fetches and decodes every source its loading clips name (current tracks and undo/redo states) once a decode context is attached (an engine with an adapter attaches `adapter.audioContext`; otherwise `attachDecodeContext(arrangement, getContext)`, or the engine option `attachDecodeContext: false` to do it yourself), then replaces each loading clip with an `AudioClip` of the same id (not an undo step). `arrangement.sources` is a `ValueSource` of `{ sources: Map<src, { status: 'pending' | 'loaded' | 'failed', error? }>, pendingCount, failedCount, isLoading }`; `arrangement.retry(src)` restarts a source whose load failed; `createArrangement({ loadSource })` replaces the exported `defaultLoadSource` (fetch + `decodeAudioData`). `getState().tracks`, `getState().duration` and the tracks an adapter receives leave loading clips out; the engine's own `setTracks`/`addTrack`/`updateTrack` take `ClipTrack` (loaded clips only). Seek/play beyond audio duration is supported (silence where there's no audio).
- `@waveform-playlist/playout` — Audio playback: Tone.js adapter (implements PlayoutAdapter from engine), global AudioContext. Peer `tone ^15.0.0`: stable (`npm install tone`, 15.1.x) is the default; the prerelease line (`npm install tone@next`, 15.5.x) is also supported and CI-tested, and is the one on which `configureGlobalContext({ sampleRate })` is honoured on the default (non-native) context. Incremental track updates via updateTrack/replaceClips — no full playout rebuild on clip operations. Optional adapter methods: addTrack, removeTrack, updateTrack, setTrackPanLaw. The SoundFont can be provided or swapped after setup via `adapter.setSoundFontCache()` on the adapter returned by `createToneAdapter()` (the React provider forwards late `soundFontCache` prop changes automatically; construct caches with `SoundFontCache.fromUrl(url)`).
- `@waveform-playlist/ui-components` — Styled primitives, theming, virtual scrolling contexts, playhead components, PlaylistErrorBoundary, BeatsAndBarsProvider
- `@waveform-playlist/annotations` — `AnnotationProvider` (hands the annotation box and text list components to `@waveform-playlist/browser`), those components (`AnnotationBox`, `AnnotationBoxesWrapper`, `AnnotationText`: `store?: AnnotationStore` is where its text, id and action edits are written, found by id; without it the list is read-only; `onAnnotationUpdate` is removed), the four annotation controls bound to the playlist provider (`ContinuousPlayCheckbox`, `LinkEndpointsCheckbox`, `EditableCheckbox`: props `className` and `children` = the label; `DownloadAnnotationsButton`: props `filename`, `disabled`, `className`, `children` = the label, `title` = the tooltip; every string the four draw can be supplied by the app; they work under either playlist provider, need no `AnnotationProvider`, have no controlled form and are not exported by `@waveform-playlist/browser`), the Aeneas parser (`parseAeneas` / `serializeAeneas`, one fragment / one annotation per call). The annotation keyboard controls are in `@waveform-playlist/browser` (`<KeyboardShortcuts annotations />`, `useAnnotationKeyboardControls`)
- `@waveform-playlist/recording` — Microphone access, AudioWorklet recording, VU meter, integrated recording hook, mic-unplug detection
- `@waveform-playlist/worklets` — Shared AudioWorklet processors: `meter-processor` (sample-accurate peak/RMS metering) and `recording-processor` (multi-channel audio capture). Auto-installed with recording package.
- `@waveform-playlist/webaudio-peaks` — Peak extraction from AudioBuffer
- `@waveform-playlist/media-element-playout` — HTMLAudioElement playback with pitch-preserving speed control, optional Web Audio routing for fades and Tone.js effect bridging
- `@dawcore/components` — Web Components for multi-track audio editing (Lit-based). Elements: `<daw-editor>`, `<daw-track>`, `<daw-clip>`, `<daw-waveform>`, `<daw-playhead>`, `<daw-ruler>`, `<daw-selection>`, `<daw-track-controls>`, `<daw-grid>` (beats/bars grid), `<daw-piano-roll>` (MIDI), `<daw-spectrogram>` (per-track FFT via `render-mode="spectrogram"`), `<daw-transport>` + transport buttons (`<daw-play-button>`, `<daw-pause-button>`, `<daw-stop-button>`, `<daw-record-button>`), `<daw-time-display>`, `<daw-time-format>`, `<daw-keyboard-shortcuts>`, `<daw-annotation-track>` + `<daw-annotation>` (declarative annotation timeline lane — reflected `start`/`end`, drag boundary editing, `keyboard-controls` navigation) + `<daw-annotation-list for="trackId">` (linked text-panel dual view, same underlying data), and `<daw-player>` (lightweight single-track HTMLMediaElement player on `@waveform-playlist/media-element-playout` — no engine/adapter/AudioContext required). Framework-agnostic — works in any framework or vanilla HTML. No Tone.js dependency; uses native Web Audio via `@dawcore/transport`. Consumer supplies a `PlayoutAdapter` (no default). Unified effects chains: `addEffect`/`removeEffect`/`setEffectParams`/`setEffectBypassed`/`moveEffect`/`effects` on `<daw-track>` (per-track chain) and `<daw-editor>` (master chain), with built-in `native-*` effects (gain, compressor, stereo panner, delay, and one type per biquad filter shape: `native-filter` = lowpass, `native-highpass`, `native-bandpass`, `native-notch`, `native-peaking`, `native-lowshelf`, `native-highshelf`), custom registration via `registerEffect` from `@waveform-playlist/core` (`@dawcore/components` no longer exports `registerEffect`, `getEffectDefinitions`, `prepareEffect`, `createEffectInstance` or the definition types — import them from `@waveform-playlist/core`, where the types are `NativeEffectDefinition`, `NativeEffectInstance`, `EffectParamDef`; definitions may declare an async `prepare(audioContext)` hook for AudioWorklet-backed effects — awaited by `exportAudio()`/`setEffectsState()`; call `editor.prepareEffect(type)` before the synchronous `addEffect`), and `daw-effect-add/remove/change/bypass/reorder` events. WAM 2.0 plugins join the same chains via `addWamPlugin(url)` (optional `@dawcore/wam` peer); Faust DSP source compiles in the browser into the same chains via `addFaustEffect(dspCode, {name?})` (optional `@dawcore/faust` peer — entries persist as `{kind:'wam', faustDsp, faustName, state}` and recompile on restore/export; compile errors keep Faust's line/column diagnostics and leave the chain untouched). Effect GUIs: `openEffectGui(effectId, container)`/`closeEffectGui(effectId)` on both elements mount a WAM plugin's own GUI (or a generic parameter panel for GUI-less plugins and `native-*` effects) into a consumer-provided container — close hides without interrupting audio, the element is cached for reopen, and the GUI is destroyed only when the effect is removed. Persistence: `getEffectsState()`/`setEffectsState(entries)` on both elements serialize/restore chains (WAM entries carry the plugin's getState snapshot; an unreachable saved URL becomes a bypassed passthrough placeholder + `daw-effect-error`, restore continues). Offline export: `editor.exportAudio({sampleRate?, startTime?, duration?, channels?})` renders the session through all chains on an OfflineAudioContext (WAM plugins re-instantiated offline with saved state) and resolves to an AudioBuffer. Runnable WAM demo: `examples/dawcore-wam/` (`pnpm example:dawcore-wam`). Vertical track reordering: `<daw-editor track-reordering>` shows a drag grip + move up/down buttons on `<daw-track-controls>`; `editor.reorderTrack(trackId, toIndex)` moves programmatically. DOM order is the visual authority (moving a `<daw-track>` element syncs the engine); undoable. Mixer moves are undo steps (#843): one per `<daw-track-controls>` slider drag or key press (`daw-track-control` detail `{ trackId, prop, value, gesture? }`), Mute or Solo click, `<daw-track>` attribute update (`daw-track-update` detail `{ trackId, changed }`; only the named mixer properties are sent) or `editor.updateTrack()` call; the controls and `editor.tracks` show the arrangement's mix and follow Undo; the editor does not write the element back. A take mutes the track it records onto (`engine.setTrackRecording`; `<daw-track-controls>` property `recording` disables its Mute button): it plays muted and shows muted, no undo step, its own mute is kept, and the exported `RecordingSession` type no longer has `armedPrevMuted`.
- `@dawcore/midi` — Framework-agnostic MIDI: the parser (`parseMidiFile`, `parseMidiUrl` — pure functions, no React) and `loadMidiTracks`, which converts a .mid file to `ClipTrack[]` with `midiNotes` for an arrangement (React apps add its tracks to the arrangement `WaveformPlaylistProvider` plays), for piano roll visualization and SoundFont/PolySynth playback. Used by `@dawcore/components` via dynamic import inside `editor.loadMidi()`. It replaces `@waveform-playlist/midi`, which is no longer published (upgrade guide: "`@waveform-playlist/midi` is replaced by `@dawcore/midi`"; the removed `useMidiTracks` hook: "`useMidiTracks` is removed: load with `loadMidiTracks`").
- `@waveform-playlist/spectrogram` — Optional spectrogram package (v13+): React `SpectrogramProvider` + UI (menu items, settings modal) integrating via `SpectrogramIntegrationContext`. Computation/worker/orchestrator are imported from `@dawcore/spectrogram`.
- `@dawcore/spectrogram` — Framework-agnostic FFT computation, Web Worker, and `SpectrogramOrchestrator` class (viewport classification, 3-tier render, generation-based abort, contiguous chunk grouping, color LUT cache). The computation and the worker pool are shared by the React Provider and the dawcore elements; `SpectrogramOrchestrator` is used by the dawcore elements only.
- `@dawcore/transport` — Native Web Audio transport (no Tone.js; its only dependency is `@waveform-playlist/core`): scheduler, clock, tempo/meter map, metronome, loop, meter-aware `quantizeTick`, a Worker-driven timer (keeps scheduling in hidden tabs) and a per-tick `tick` event for consumers that must poll the playhead off rAF. Replaces Tone.js Transport for the dawcore stack. Implements the `PlayoutAdapter` interface from `@waveform-playlist/engine` via `NativePlayoutAdapter`. Exposes effects insertion hooks (`connectTrackEffects(trackId, input, output)` — a PRE-FADER track insert: clips → effects → volume → pan → mute — and `connectMasterOutput`) used by the dawcore effects chains. Track effects are pre-fader in every renderer (web components, React/Tone, and both offline exports): the fader never changes how hard a compressor works.
- `@dawcore/faust` — ONLY for live (in-browser) Faust compilation; for effects known at build time, precompile instead (guide: /docs/faust-effects — `faust2wasm` + `registerEffect` (from `@waveform-playlist/core`)/`prepare` for an AudioWorklet effect, loaded with `track.addEffect(id)` in web components or `addEffect(id)` in React, or `faust2wam` + `addWamPlugin(url)`/`addWamEffect(url)` for a WAM plugin; serve the compiled folder as static files, never through the bundler). Licences: `@dawcore/faust` is MIT but loads `@shren/faust2wam` (LGPL-3.0), whose bundle includes the faustwasm runtime (LGPL) and faust-ui (GPL-3.0-or-later); precompiled output still ships the LGPL faustwasm runtime, and `faust2wam` output includes faust-ui unless removed. In-browser Faust DSP compilation to WAM 2.0 plugins: `compileFaustToWam(dspCode, {name?})` wraps `@shren/faust2wam`'s generate() with a cached lazy compiler load (the ~2.5 MB gzipped libfaust WASM ships inside the dependency, loaded on first compile only). Returns `{factory, name, dspCode}` — the factory instantiates via `@dawcore/wam`'s `createWamInstanceFromFactory`. Faust compile errors propagate unchanged with line/column diagnostics. Optional peer of `@dawcore/components` — dynamic-imported by `addFaustEffect()`, so non-Faust users load zero compiler bytes.
- `@dawcore/wam` — Web Audio Modules (WAM 2.0) plugin hosting: idempotent host initialization (`ensureWamHost`), plugin loading/validation (`createWamInstance` from a URL or `createWamInstanceFromFactory` from an already-obtained WebAudioModule class, both with optional `createGui`/`destroyGui` passthroughs), library manifest discovery (`fetchWamLibrary` — webaudiomodules.com community registry and pedalboard2/wam-studio manifest shapes, `baseUrl` option for registry-relative paths), plain-DOM GUI helpers (`createParameterPanel`, `createWamParameterPanel` — generic slider panels from parameter metadata, themable via `--daw-*` CSS custom properties), transport sync (`createWamTransportBridge` — broadcasts `wam-transport` events with tempo/timeSig/bar/playing to plugin nodes on every transport event and, via the transport's Worker-driven `tick` event, on variable-tempo boundary crossings and loop wraps — no rAF, so plugins stay in sync in a hidden tab), and offline cloning (`cloneInstanceInto` — re-instantiates a plugin on an OfflineAudioContext with its getState snapshot, used by `exportAudio`). Optional peer of `@dawcore/components` — dynamic-imported by `addWamPlugin()`/`openEffectGui()`, so non-WAM users load zero WAM bytes.

## Requirements and Upgrading

- The React packages (`@waveform-playlist/browser`, `ui-components`, `annotations`, `spectrogram`, `recording`) require `react` and `react-dom` `^19.0.0` and `styled-components` `^6.0.0`.
- Upgrading from an earlier major: follow https://naomiaro.github.io/waveform-playlist/docs/react/upgrading — it lists every breaking change with a Find / Replace-with entry, written so a coding agent can apply it mechanically.

## Quick Start

```tsx
import {
  WaveformPlaylistProvider,
  Waveform,
  PlayButton,
  PauseButton,
  StopButton,
  useCreateArrangement,
} from '@waveform-playlist/browser';
import { audioTrack } from '@waveform-playlist/core';

function App() {
  // The arrangement owns the tracks and loads their audio once the provider has an adapter.
  const arrangement = useCreateArrangement(() => [
    audioTrack({ src: '/audio/track1.mp3', name: 'Track 1' }),
    audioTrack({ src: '/audio/track2.mp3', name: 'Track 2' }),
  ]);

  return (
    <WaveformPlaylistProvider arrangement={arrangement}>
      <PlayButton /> <PauseButton /> <StopButton />
      <Waveform />
    </WaveformPlaylistProvider>
  );
}
```

Change tracks through the arrangement (`arrangement.addTrack(audioTrack({ src: file }))`, `removeTrack`, `updateTrack`, `setTracks`; below the provider `useArrangement()` returns it), from a handler, an effect or an `arrangement.sources` listener, not from inside `arrangement.subscribe()` or an engine `statechange` listener. Loading state: `useArrangementSources(arrangement)`. Play does nothing until the first ready (`usePlaylistTimeline().isReady`, `onReady`, the `waveform-playlist:ready` window event, once per mount).

## Web Components Quick Start

No React and no build step — drop `<daw-editor>` into any HTML page and assign a `PlayoutAdapter`:

```html
<script type="module">
  import '@dawcore/components';
  import { NativePlayoutAdapter } from '@dawcore/transport';

  const editor = document.querySelector('daw-editor');
  editor.adapter = new NativePlayoutAdapter(new AudioContext());
</script>

<daw-editor id="editor" samples-per-pixel="1024" wave-height="100" timescale>
  <daw-track src="/audio/drums.opus" name="Drums"></daw-track>
  <daw-track src="/audio/bass.opus" name="Bass"></daw-track>
</daw-editor>

<daw-transport for="editor">
  <daw-play-button></daw-play-button>
  <daw-pause-button></daw-pause-button>
  <daw-stop-button></daw-stop-button>
</daw-transport>
```

`<daw-editor>` does not create an `AudioContext` — you own it and assign a `PlayoutAdapter`: `NativePlayoutAdapter` (from `@dawcore/transport`) for native Web Audio, or a Tone.js adapter (from `@waveform-playlist/playout`) when you need MIDI playback.

`<daw-editor>` owns an arrangement (`createArrangement()` from `@waveform-playlist/engine`) and builds its engine on it once the adapter is set; `<daw-track>` elements wait for the adapter, then enter in DOM order and their audio loads through the arrangement. Loading never clears the undo history, and the page's own `<daw-track>` elements that enter while the history is empty are not undo steps. `editor.addTrack(config)` resolves with the track id once the track has entered, before its audio loads; add the `daw-track-ready` / `daw-track-error` listener BEFORE calling it, because for a track with nothing to fetch (or whose audio is already loaded) the event fires before the promise resolves. `daw-track-ready` means the audio has loaded (peaks are drawn a moment later) and fires again each time the track has loaded again. A track whose audio failed stays (its clip drawn failed where its length is known: a `duration` or `peaks-src`) until `editor.retryTrack(trackId)` loads it or the app removes it.

**Driving `<daw-editor>` from code or an AI agent: `editor.arrangement`.** It is the arrangement the editor plays (tracks, clips, mix, undo/redo, loading; the engine guide's "The Arrangement" lists its methods). Read it and call it, or hand one in: `editor.arrangement = createArrangement({ tracks })` plays that one alone (the `<daw-track>` children are not added to it and show `:state(detached)`; `null` goes back to the editor's own, with its history). A swap keeps the adapter. The editor's methods (`addTrack`, `updateTrack`, `reorderTrack`, `addClip`, `updateClip`, `removeTrack`, `removeClip`) are arrangement calls on the one played: `addTrack` and `addClip` create no element, and only `removeTrack` / `removeClip` touch an element (they remove it). `reorderTrack(id, toIndex)` takes an index in the arrangement's order. `<daw-track>` / `<daw-clip>` attributes are the page's declaration and are never written by the editor; their properties (`trackEl.volume`, `clipEl.start`, `trackEl.index`) read the arrangement live. A change an agent makes to the arrangement during a user's drag cancels the drag when it touches the dragged clip or track (both editors). A split keeps the clip's id on its left half.

## Architecture

Both providers use React Context with small contexts for performance (22 public hooks: 11 that both providers serve, 9 that only WaveformPlaylistProvider serves, 2 that only MediaElementPlaylistProvider serves). Each hook returns one group of fields that change together, and a component re-renders only for the hooks it calls. A hook reads the NEAREST playlist provider.

**Under either provider** (a component written against these works with both):
1. **useIsPlaying()** — isPlaying; changes on play, pause, stop
2. **useCurrentTime()** — currentTime: where the cursor rests; changes on seek, pause, stop and a leftward selection drag, does not advance during playback
3. **useSelection()** — selectionStart, selectionEnd; changes on every pointer move of a selection drag
4. **useActiveAnnotation()** — activeAnnotationId; changes at every annotation boundary during playback
5. **useAnnotations()** — annotations: the provider's annotation store's list, `readonly AnnotationData[]` (frozen in development; `[]` without an `annotationStore` prop) (NOT activeAnnotationId, NOT the options)
6. **useAnnotationOptions()** — editable, linkEndpoints, continuousPlay: provider state under both providers. Each starts from the provider's `annotationList` prop (`editable`, `linkEndpoints`, `isContinuousPlay`; a field left out is false) and takes the field's new value when it changes; set with setAnnotationsEditable / setLinkEndpoints / setContinuousPlay of usePlaybackControls(), or the three checkboxes of `@waveform-playlist/annotations`
7. **usePlaybackControls()** — changes only when the `annotationStore` prop does: play(start?, duration?) / pause / stop / seekTo (stop returns the cursor to where playback started; seekTo clamps to the audio and restarts a running play), setSelection, setTimeFormat, setAutomaticScroll, setScrollContainer, scrollContainerRef, setContinuousPlay, setAnnotationsEditable, setLinkEndpoints, annotationStore (the provider's `annotationStore` prop, or undefined: change the annotations with its set / update; `setAnnotations` is removed), setActiveAnnotationId, playAnnotation(annotation) (what a click on a box or a list row does: makes it active and plays it; ends with the annotation when continuous play is off), annotationPreview (a source: the annotations as an edge drag in progress would leave them)
8. **usePlaybackRefs()** — never re-renders: currentTimeRef (live position), visualTimeRef (the position to draw), registerFrameCallback / unregisterFrameCallback. Read `.current` in handlers, effects and frame callbacks; to re-render when a value changes, also call the hook that carries it
9. **usePlaylistView()** — what the provider was configured with that a view also reads: sampleRate, mono, indefinitePlayback (the last two always false under MediaElementPlaylistProvider). The view options (waveHeight, barWidth, barGap, roundedBars, progressBarWidth, fillViewport) are NOT here: they are props of `<WaveformViewOptions>`, and a component inside a root reads the resolved values with `usePlaylistInfo()` from `@waveform-playlist/ui-components`; changes on a prop change (and once when the real sample rate is known), not on a settings click
10. **usePlaylistSettings()** — timeFormat, isAutomaticScroll; changes when the user changes either (apart from the view value, which every clip overlay and the visualization read)
11. **usePlaylistZoom()** — samplesPerPixel, canZoomIn, canZoomOut (both always false under MediaElementPlaylistProvider); changes on a zoom

**WaveformPlaylistProvider only** (multi-track, Web Audio API; these throw when the nearest provider is MediaElementPlaylistProvider):
1. **useArrangement()** — never changes: the provider's `Arrangement` (tracks, mix, undo history, loading); change tracks through it
2. **useEditorControls()** — never changes: setCurrentTime, setTrackMute / setTrackSolo / setTrackVolume / setTrackPan / setTrackPanLaw (first argument is the track ID, not an index; a non-string is ignored), reorderTrack(trackId, toIndex), setSelectedTrackId, zoomIn / zoomOut, setMasterVolume, loop setters, undo / redo, setRecordingActive. The mixer setters, reorderTrack, undo and redo call the arrangement and work with no engine attached; each mixer call is an undo step, and undo brings back the mix. The setters take a last `options?: MixerChangeOptions` (from `@waveform-playlist/engine`): `{ gesture: id }` makes the calls of one slider drag one step (one `createMixerGesture()` from `@waveform-playlist/core` per slider, `gesture.attach(input)` in an effect; the built-in sliders do this), `{ undoable: false }` is no step (automation, a restored mix). Keyboard Undo does not fire while a slider has focus (#730)
3. **useEngineRefs()** — never re-renders: playoutRef (PlaylistEngine), playbackStartTimeRef, audioStartPositionRef, getPlaybackTime, getAudioContextTime, getLookAhead, getOutputLatency
4. **usePlaylistTimeline()** — tracks (`readonly ClipTrack[]`: the arrangement's tracks without clips still loading; never write to them), peaksDataArray (one row per track; a row also holds placeholder records, `isPlaceholder: true`, of clips still loading: find a record by clipId, never by position), duration (loaded audio only), isReady (false until an engine is attached and the first sources have settled, then false only while a later engine is built; a source that never settles, e.g. a hanging request with no load timeout yet (#840), keeps it false and Play does nothing: show `useArrangementSources(arrangement).pendingCount`/`isLoading` meanwhile); changes on every clip operation (a trim once, on release), a zoom (peaksDataArray is computed per zoom level), audio or peaks arriving, isReady changing (call it in the smallest component that needs it). `onTracksChange` is removed
5. **usePlaylistMixer()** — trackStates (one entry per track in the order of `tracks`, for every track from the moment it enters the arrangement, no `undefined` entries; the arrangement's mix by track id, so a track keeps its mute/solo/volume/pan/panLaw when tracks are removed, added or reordered), masterVolume; changes on every mute, solo, volume, pan or pan-law change (each step of a slider drag; also when a track's first audio decides its pan law) and when tracks are added, removed, renamed or reordered (same advice)
6. **useTrackReorderPreview()** — trackDragPreview; changes on every drag-over of a track reorder
7. **useLoop()** — isLoopEnabled, loopStart, loopEnd
8. **useSelectedTrackId()** — selectedTrackId
9. **useUndoRedo()** — canUndo, canRedo; changes after an edit
10. **useTrack()** — ONLY among the children of `<WaveformTrackControls>` (throws elsewhere): the track whose control panel is being drawn: id, kind, index, name, muted, soloed, volume, pan, panLaw ('auto' until the track's first decoded audio decides it, then 'mono' or 'stereo'; a track keeps its law whatever clips follow), renderMode, isSelected, isFirst, isLast, hasSpectrogram, isRecording (a take is being recorded onto it: it plays muted and `muted` is true, its TrackMuteButton disabled; `isLoading` is removed, the controls work while a track loads), and bound actions setMuted, setSoloed, setVolume, setPan, setPanLaw('mono' | 'stereo') (undo steps; each takes the same `options` as the setters of useEditorControls), select, moveUp, moveDown, setRenderMode, openSpectrogramSettings; changes when that track's state, position or selection changes

**MediaElementPlaylistProvider only** (single-track, HTMLAudioElement; these throw when the nearest provider is WaveformPlaylistProvider):
1. **usePlaybackRate()** — playbackRate (0.5 to 2), setPlaybackRate
2. **useMediaElementTrack()** — duration (from the waveform data, known at first render), isReady (media metadata loaded; do not gate Play on it), peaksDataArray (its one clip carries the track's fadeIn / fadeOut), playoutRef (MediaElementPlayout)

Each hook's value type is exported (`PlaybackControlsContextValue`, `PlaylistViewContextValue`, …), as are `ClipPeaks`, `TrackClipPeaks`, `TrackDragPreview` and `FrameData`. `ClipPeaks.isPlaceholder` (required boolean) is true for the record of a clip whose audio is still loading; such a record is drawn by `Clip` without a drag handle and without trim handles, drawn dimmed: the whole clip container, header included, gets `opacity` from the theme key `placeholderClipOpacity` (optional; 0.5 when the theme does not set it or sets something that is not a number from 0 to 1), and its container carries `data-clip-placeholder="true"` (an app can restyle it with CSS of its own). `WaveformPlaylistProvider` produces a placeholder record for a clip still loading that has a `duration` or `waveformData` (drawn from its peaks; with only a `duration`, as a box of the clip's extent in the waveform's bar colour: `<ClipPlaceholderBody />` from `@waveform-playlist/ui-components`, `data-clip-placeholder-body="true"`; a clip that names only its `src` draws nothing until loaded), once it has a sample rate (the `sampleRate` prop's, a request, then the first adapter's context rate); `MediaElementPlaylistProvider` sets it to `false` on every record. An app that builds a `ClipPeaks` object adds `isPlaceholder: false`. `Clip` (`@waveform-playlist/ui-components`) takes the matching `isPlaceholder?: boolean` (default false).

Library controls that work under either provider: PlayButton, PauseButton, StopButton (disabled unless playing), RewindButton, FastForwardButton (disabled with indefinitePlayback), SkipBackwardButton, SkipForwardButton, ClearAllButton, AudioPosition, TimeFormatSelect, SelectionTimeInputs, AutomaticScrollCheckbox, AnnotationList (draws nothing without AnnotationProvider), and from `@waveform-playlist/annotations` ContinuousPlayCheckbox, LinkEndpointsCheckbox, EditableCheckbox and DownloadAnnotationsButton (no AnnotationProvider needed). MediaElementPlaylistProvider only: PlaybackRateSelect. WaveformPlaylistProvider only: LoopButton, SetLoopRegionButton, ZoomInButton, ZoomOutButton, MasterVolumeControl, KeyboardShortcuts, ExportWavButton.

Removed: `usePlaylistControls()`, `usePlaylistAnnotations()`, `useMediaElementAnimation()`, `useMediaElementState()`, `useMediaElementControls()` and `useMediaElementData()` are no longer exported, and before them the combined data / state / animation hooks. `usePlaybackRefs()` keeps its name; its eight engine fields are on `useEngineRefs()`, and the `usePlaybackRefs()` value is a plain object, so a leftover read of one of them is `undefined`. `PlayheadProps` (what a `renderPlayhead` function receives) is the same seven props under both providers: `position`, `color`, `isPlaying`, `currentTimeRef`, `visualTimeRef`, `samplesPerPixel`, `sampleRate`; `getPlaybackTime`, `getAudioContextTime`, `playbackStartTimeRef`, `audioStartPositionRef` and `controlsOffset` are removed from it. The upgrade guide (https://naomiaro.github.io/waveform-playlist/docs/react/upgrading) has a field-to-hook table for each.

## Key Hooks

*From `@waveform-playlist/browser` (core, engine-free):*
- `useCreateAnnotationStore(init?, { beforeChange? })` — The `AnnotationStore` (from `@waveform-playlist/core`) that owns an editor's annotations, one per component instance; pass it to either provider's `annotationStore` prop. `init` is read once (a refused list throws to the error boundary). `beforeChange(next, current)` returns the list to store: `next` accepts, `current` refuses (nobody is told), another list adjusts; the latest committed render's function is called; it is not called for an `update` that returns `current` nor for a list that fails validation (checked first). The store: `getAnnotations()` (the same array until a change; never write to it), `subscribe(listener)` (returns unsubscribe), `set(list)`, `update(fn)`; both apply before they return, so two updates in one tick both land; an `update` that returns `current` notifies nobody. Every list is checked in every build (finite numeric `start`/`end`, unique ids): otherwise a `TypeError` and the store keeps its value. In a development build (`process.env.NODE_ENV` set and not 'production') the list, each annotation and its `lines` are frozen: `.sort()` throws, a field assignment throws in strict code (modules). `createAnnotationStore(initial?, options?)` from core is the same without React. `useStoredAnnotations(store)` reads it (re-renders on a change; works above the provider). To persist: `store.subscribe(...)`, or `useStoredAnnotations(store)` in an effect. `onAnnotationsChange` and `annotationList.annotations` are removed
- `useAnnotationDragHandlers({ store, preview?, samplesPerPixel, sampleRate?, duration, linkEndpoints })` — Drag handlers for annotation box edges; `store` (usePlaybackControls().annotationStore) replaces `annotations` + `onAnnotationsChange`, and without it the handlers do nothing. The drag keeps the bounds of every annotation it touched (also one moved back) and works out each move over the store's current list with them on top (a neighbour moved elsewhere during the drag collides where it is now). Pass `preview: annotationPreview` (from `usePlaybackControls()`, under either provider) and each move is published to the preview (so a change made elsewhere shows at once) while the store is written once, on release: the touched `start`/`end`, by id, onto the store's list as it is then (an annotation added during the drag stays); without `preview`, every move writes them. Escape restores every annotation the drag touched (with `preview` nothing is written). The drag ends, writing nothing more and clearing the preview, when the dragged annotation is removed from the store (also "clear all"), when the store changes, or on unmount. `useAnnotationsWithPreview(annotations, annotationPreview)` returns what to draw in a custom annotation renderer. `WaveformAnnotationBoxes` calls the hook itself inside its own `DragDropProvider`: use it only for a row of boxes you draw yourself.
- `useClipDragHandlers({ snapSamplePosition? })` (the options are optional) — Drag-to-move and boundary trimming on the provider's arrangement at its zoom level (both read from context; options `tracks`, `engineRef` and `samplesPerPixel` removed; throws outside WaveformPlaylistProvider): arrangement.moveClip()/trimClip() on release (one undo step each). A trim is previewed in the view while dragged (the tracks do not change until release); Escape changes nothing. a move or trim commits the clip and track picked up at drag start (by id); draggable ids are `clip/<trackId>/<clipId>` and `clip-boundary-left|right/<trackId>/<clipId>`; a move or trim made while no engine is attached is kept and the next engine plays it
- `useDragSensors(opts?)` — Configures PointerSensor activation constraints for DragDropProvider (distance-based default, optional touch-optimized mode)
- `ClipCollisionModifier` — Collision detection modifier for clip moves, prevents overlapping clips
- `SnapToGridModifier` — Snap-to-grid modifier for clip moves. Two modes: `'beats'` (PPQN tick grid) and `'timescale'` (sample-based grid). Snaps absolute position, not delta.
- `useClipSplitting()` — Split clips at playhead: one arrangement.splitClip() on the provider's arrangement, snapped at its zoom level (both read from context; no options: `tracks`, `engineRef` and `samplesPerPixel` removed; throws outside WaveformPlaylistProvider), kept with no engine attached. Returns `splitClipAtPlayhead()` and `splitClipAt(trackId, clipId, splitTime)` (ids, not indexes; an unknown id or a clip still loading returns false)
- `useKeyboardShortcuts(opts)` — Custom keyboard shortcuts
- `usePlaybackShortcuts(opts)` — Default playback shortcuts (Space, Escape, 0). WaveformPlaylistProvider only (throws under MediaElementPlaylistProvider). Shortcuts never take a key the focused control uses, however it got focus: inputs (incl. sliders, checkboxes) and `<select>` keep all keys, Escape closes an open modal dialog, Space/Enter go to a focused `<button>` or `<summary>` (Enter only for a link) (after clicking Mute, Space toggles Mute; Space is play/pause when focus is not on a control)
- `KeyboardShortcuts` — Self-closing component for declarative keyboard shortcut setup. Props: `playback` (Space/Escape/0), `clipSplitting` ('s' key), `annotations` (arrows / Home / End select an annotation, Escape deselects, Enter plays it, `[` `]` move its start and Shift+`[` Shift+`]` its end by 10 ms; through the provider's annotation store, the active annotation found by id when the key is pressed; the hook is `useAnnotationKeyboardControls({ store, activeAnnotationId, … })`), `undo` (Cmd/Ctrl+Z, Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Z; they, and `useEditorControls().undo/redo`, do nothing during a clip or track drag), `additionalShortcuts`. Escape during a drag only cancels the drag. All booleans default to false. Reads all required data from context.

*From `@waveform-playlist/browser/tone` (Tone.js batteries-included):*
- `useDynamicEffects()` — Master effects chain with runtime add/remove/reorder/bypass/parameter updates. Returns `effects` (a `ValueSource<ActiveEffect[]>`, NOT an `activeEffects` array: read it with `useActiveEffects(effects)`), `availableEffects`, `addEffect(id): Promise<string>` (resolves with the instanceId; rejects for an unknown id), `addWamEffect(url)`, `removeEffect`, `updateParameter`, `toggleBypass`, `reorderEffects`, `clearAllEffects`, `masterEffects` (pass to the provider's `effects` prop), `createOfflineEffectsFunction()` (always returns a function, the same one on every call; it reads the chain when the export runs), `analyserRef`. The hook does not re-render when the chain changes and everything it returns is identity-stable. Call it ONCE and pass the result down (a second call creates a second, empty chain). `availableEffects` = the built-ins plus, only in native-context mode, registered custom types; it is read when the calling component renders (not subscribed), so register custom effects before the component that shows the picker renders. The chain survives a StrictMode remount, Fast Refresh and a hidden `<Activity>` (no cleanup on unmount): add defaults on mount behind a ref guard; instances of an unmounted chain are disposed when it is garbage-collected (best effort), or at a known moment by `clearAllEffects()`, which also rejects any add still in flight ("aborted: the effects chain was cleared")
- `useTrackDynamicEffects()` — Per-track effects management. Returns `getTrackEffects(trackId)` (a `ValueSource<TrackActiveEffect[]>` per track, NOT a `trackEffectsState` map: read it with `useActiveEffects(getTrackEffects(trackId))`), `addEffectToTrack(trackId, id): Promise<string>`, `addWamEffectToTrack`, `removeEffectFromTrack`, `updateTrackEffectParameter`, `toggleBypass(trackId, instanceId)`, `reorderTrackEffects(trackId, fromIndex, toIndex)`, `clearTrackEffects(trackId)` (disposes that track's effects and rejects its adds still in flight; chains are not disposed on unmount, same lifetime as the master chain), `getTrackEffectsFunction(trackId)` (same function per track id, never undefined; pass the function itself to the provider: `<WaveformPlaylistProvider trackEffects={getTrackEffectsFunction}>`. Tracks have no `effects` field: never copy track objects to attach effects. For a fixed function per track, give the track an `id` (`audioTrack({ id, src })`) and key the lookup on it), `createOfflineTrackEffectsFunction(trackId)` (never undefined), `availableEffects`
- `useActiveEffects(source)` — Subscribes a component to one effects chain and returns `ActiveEffect[]`. Call it in the component that draws the rack, not at the page root; that component re-renders when the chain changes
- Custom effects in React — register an AudioWorklet or native-node effect with `registerEffect(id, definition)` from `@waveform-playlist/core` (definition: `label`, `category`, `defaults`, `params`, `create(audioContext, params)`, optional async `prepare(audioContext)` and `wetParam`), then `addEffect(id)` / `addEffectToTrack(trackId, id)`. Requires native-context mode (`configureGlobalContext({ nativeAudioContext: true })` from `@waveform-playlist/playout` before any audio initialization, as for WAM; otherwise the add rejects). `prepare` is awaited by `addEffect` on the live context and by WAV export on the offline context. Parameters are numeric (`updateParameter` ignores a non-number for a custom effect). The host owns every connection out of the instance's `output` and disconnects all of them on a rewire: do not connect `output` to anything inside the effect. An AudioWorklet effect's `dispose` should tell the processor to stop over its port (do not return `false` from `process()` while the effect may be reconnected: a bypassed-by-disconnection processor did not restart in Chrome). If the chain cannot be rewired with the new effect, the previous chain is restored and the add rejects. Bypass zeroes `wetParam` when the definition has one, otherwise disconnects the effect. Entries have `kind: 'custom'` (`ActiveEffect.kind` is `'tone' | 'wam' | 'custom'`; `'tone'` = built-in Tone.js effect, called `'native'` before the next major; `<daw-editor>`'s own `kind: 'native'` is a different type and unchanged). Guide: /docs/react/guides/effects#custom-effects `availableEffects` lists the Tone.js effects and the app's own registered types; `@dawcore/components`' `native-*` effects (marked `builtIn` in the shared registry) are left out of it but can be added by id.
- `useExportWav()` — Offline WAV export with effects support
- `useOutputMeter(options?)` — Real-time master output VU meter. Returns `{ meter, resetPeak, error }`; `meter` is a `MeterSource` (`subscribe` / `getSnapshot` over `{ levels, peakLevels, rmsLevels }`), not state, so the hook does not re-render as levels change. Draw it with `<SegmentedVUMeter meter={meter} />`
- `useMasterAnalyser(fftSize?)` — FFT analyser wired in parallel to the master output. Returns `{ analyserRef, masterEffects }` — pass `masterEffects` to the provider's `effects` prop and read frequency data from `analyserRef.current`
- `ExportWavButton` — Pre-built button component wired to useExportWav
- `effectDefinitions`, `effectCategories`, `getEffectDefinition`, `getEffectsByCategory`, `createToneEffectInstance(definition, initialParams?)` (named `createEffectInstance` before; core's `createEffectInstance` is the registry's, a different function), `createEffectChain` — Factory and definitions for the built-in Tone.js effects. Chorus, tremolo, auto panner and auto filter are returned with their LFO started (do not call `start()` on the node again). An `EffectInstance` has `input` and `output` nodes (not `effect`). `getAvailableEffects()` lists the built-ins followed, in native-context mode only, by registered custom types (a read, not a subscription); `createCustomEffectInstance(type, audioContext, params?)` builds a registered one. The registry itself (`registerEffect`, …) is in `@waveform-playlist/core`

### Arrangement Hooks (from `@waveform-playlist/browser`, core entry)

- `useCreateArrangement(init?, options?)` — One `Arrangement` (from `@waveform-playlist/engine`) per component instance: pass it to `<WaveformPlaylistProvider arrangement>`. `init: () => readonly ArrangementTrack[]` (e.g. `() => [audioTrack({ src: '/a.mp3' })]`) and `options: { loadSource?, undoLimit? }` are read on the first render only. An initializer that throws (a track of the wrong kind, a clip still loading on a MIDI track, a duplicate track id, two clips with one id) throws out of the render to an error boundary above the calling component, not to a provider's `onError`. Under StrictMode the initializer runs twice and one result is kept. Creating an arrangement fetches nothing: the provider attaches its first adapter's AudioContext as the decode context. A new arrangement object passed to the provider remounts everything below it (warns once in development): keep one.
- `useArrangement()` — The provider's arrangement, below `WaveformPlaylistProvider` (throws elsewhere and under MediaElementPlaylistProvider); never re-renders.
- `useArrangementTracks(arrangement)` — `arrangement.getTracks()` (`readonly ArrangementTrack[]`, loading clips included); re-renders when the tracks change, not on a mix change. Argument required.
- `useArrangementSources(arrangement)` — `ArrangementSourcesValue` (`{ sources, pendingCount, failedCount, isLoading }`, each source `pending`, `loaded` or `failed` with its `error`); the same object until a status changes. Argument required. A failed source is reported here, not through the provider's `onError`; `arrangement.retry(src)` starts it again.
- Removed: `useAudioTracks`, `useDynamicTracks` and the types `AudioTrackConfig`, `TrackSource`, `TrackLoadError`, `UseDynamicTracksReturn` (from `/tone`). A track names its audio with `audioTrack({ src | audioBuffer | waveformData, name, start, duration, offset, … })` from `@waveform-playlist/core` (`start`, not `startTime`); a dropped file is `arrangement.addTrack(audioTrack({ src: file }))`. Guide: https://naomiaro.github.io/waveform-playlist/docs/react/guides/loading-audio
- The same arrangement can also be played by a `PlaylistEngine` an app builds itself (`new PlaylistEngine({ adapter, arrangement })`), one engine at a time.

### MIDI (from `@dawcore/midi`)

- `loadMidiTracks(src, options)` — A function, not a hook: `src` is a URL string, a `File` or a `Blob`; resolves to `ClipTrack[]` (`kind: 'midi'`, new ids on every call). `options: { sampleRate (required), flatten?, start? (seconds), duration? (seconds), name?, signal? }`. `name` names the track and its clip only when the file yields exactly one track. An aborted `signal` rejects with the signal's reason.
- `parseMidiFile(data, options?)` — Pure function: ArrayBuffer → ParsedMidi with tracks, notes, tempo, time signature. No React dependency.
- `parseMidiUrl(url, options?, signal?)` — Fetch + parse convenience wrapper with AbortSignal support.

### MIDI Loading (from `@dawcore/components`, requires optional `@dawcore/midi` peer dep)

- `editor.loadMidi(source, options?)` — Imperatively load a `.mid` file (URL string or File) and add N MIDI tracks (no `<daw-track>` element; drawn as piano rolls) — one per note-bearing MIDI track. Returns `Promise<MidiLoadResult>` with `{ trackIds, bpm, timeSignature, duration, name }`. Cleanup-on-failure via `Promise.allSettled`: any per-track failure removes every track the call added, with no undo step; `options.signal` cancels it the same way. Dynamic-imports `@dawcore/midi` on first call; throws friendly install hint if missing.
- `MidiLoadOptions` — `{ startTime?: number; signal?: AbortSignal }`. `signal` cancels the fetch, the parse and the tracks waiting to enter; the call rejects with its reason and takes out the tracks it added (no undo step). `addTrack(config, options?)`, `addClip(trackId, config, options?)` and `loadFiles(files, options?)` take the same `{ signal }` (`EditorCallOptions`).
- `MidiLoadResult` — `{ readonly trackIds: readonly string[]; readonly bpm: number; readonly timeSignature: readonly [number, number]; readonly duration: number; readonly name: string }`.

### Beats & Bars (from `@waveform-playlist/ui-components`)

- `BeatsAndBarsProvider` — Optional context providing BPM, time signature, and snap config. Wraps playlist content to enable beats & bars timescale mode in SmartScale. Props: `bpm`, `timeSignature: [number, number]`, `snapTo: 'bar' | 'beat' | 'off'`
- `getScaleInfo(samplesPerPixel)` — Returns `{ marker, bigStep, smallStep }` (ms) for temporal timescale tick spacing at the given zoom level. Also useful for deriving `gridSamples` for `SnapToGridModifier` temporal mode.

### Virtual Scrolling Hooks (from `@waveform-playlist/ui-components`)

- `useScrollViewport()` — Current scroll position and viewport dimensions (with 1.5x overscan buffer)
- `useVisibleChunkIndices(totalWidth, chunkWidth, originX?)` — Memoized array of visible chunk indices for canvas virtualization
- `useClipViewportOrigin()` — Clip's pixel offset in the timeline (for correct chunk visibility in multi-clip tracks)

### Recording Hooks (from `@waveform-playlist/recording`)

- `useIntegratedRecording(arrangement, selectedTrackId, options?)` — Combined recording + track management (was `(tracks, setTracks, selectedTrackId, options)`; it reads the arrangement and keeps no copy): a take is added to the track that was selected when `startRecording()` was called (returned as `recordingTrackId`, `null` when idle; the target cannot be switched mid-take, and `startRecording()` refuses, through `error`, no selected track, an id the arrangement does not hold, a MIDI track and a track holding a clip whose audio is not loaded); mic access, VU meter (`meter`, a `MeterSource`), live take progress (`progress`, a `RecordingProgressSource` to pass as `<WaveformRecordingPreview recordingState={{ isRecording: true, trackId, startSample, progress, bits: 16 }} />`, a child of `<WaveformTracks>`), start/stop/pause recording, adds the take at the record-start playhead position with punch-in replace semantics (overlapped clip content is trimmed/removed/split) in one `arrangement.updateTrack()`, one undo step; recording latency compensation is configurable via `latencyOffset` (seconds) on both the React `IntegratedRecordingOptions` and the dawcore `RecordingOptions` passed to `editor.startRecording()`. `startRecording()` resolves `true` when capture actually started. Call `useRecordingSession({ isRecording, trackId: recordingTrackId })` (from `@waveform-playlist/browser`) in the same component: the view only draws the take, and this hook tells the provider one is running. For overdub, also call `useEditorControls().setRecordingActive(true, trackId)` before `play()` — while the session is active the end-of-timeline auto-stop is suppressed (the take can run past existing audio) and the recorded-over track is marked in the arrangement as the take's (`setTrackRecording`; punch-in replaces it), which plays it muted and is no undo step: `trackStates` shows it muted, its TrackMuteButton is disabled and `useTrack().isRecording` is true, while `arrangement.getMixer()` keeps the track's own mute, so a mute changed during the take stays after it; the take's mute is cleared when the session ends, the take's track changes or the provider unmounts. `play()` does nothing before the playlist's first ready. `<daw-editor>` does both automatically during recording (no API call needed)
- `useRecording(stream, options)` — Low-level recording via AudioWorklet; `startRecording()` resolves `true`/`false` for capture start success. Elapsed time and live peaks come through `progress`, a `RecordingProgressSource` (`subscribe` / `getSnapshot` over `{ duration, peaks }`), not state
- `useRecordingProgress(progress, { updateRate? })` — A recording's `{ duration, peaks }` as React state, at most `updateRate` times a second (default 10); for an elapsed-time label
- `enumerateMicrophones()` / `watchMicrophoneDevices(listener)` — framework-agnostic, permission-free mic listing from `@waveform-playlist/core` (`hasLabels` false pre-permission: browsers redact labels)
- `useMicrophoneAccess()` — Request mic permission, enumerate devices, get MediaStream
- `useMicrophoneLevel(stream, options?)` — Real-time VU meter levels from mic stream (supports multi-channel via `channelCount` option). Returns `{ meter, resetPeak, error }`; `meter` is a `MeterSource`, not state
- `useOutputMeter(options?)` — Real-time master output VU meter (from `@waveform-playlist/browser/tone`). Returns `{ meter, resetPeak, error }`
- `useMeterLevels(meter, { updateRate? })` (from `@waveform-playlist/ui-components`) — A meter's `{ levels, peakLevels, rmsLevels }` as React state, at most `updateRate` times a second (default 10). `useThrottledValue(source, options?)` is the generic form for any `ValueSource`
- `SegmentedVUMeter` (from `@waveform-playlist/ui-components`) — LED-style meter. `meter={meter}` draws a live `MeterSource` directly to the DOM without re-rendering; `levels` / `peakLevels` props remain for values you hold yourself
- Meter levels and recording progress change ~60 times a second, so these hooks return a source (`ValueSource<T>` from `@waveform-playlist/core`: `subscribe(listener)` + `getSnapshot()`, compatible with `useSyncExternalStore`) instead of state. Migration from the old `levels` / `duration` / `recordingPeaks` fields: https://naomiaro.github.io/waveform-playlist/docs/react/upgrading

## Key Components

- `WaveformPlaylistProvider` — Multi-track provider (Web Audio API / Tone.js). **Single instance per page** (shared Tone.js Transport). Props: arrangement (required; from `useCreateArrangement`), mono (the provider computes the peaks with it), samplesPerPixel, zoomLevels, automaticScroll, theme (merged over `defaultTheme`), annotationStore (the owner of the annotations, from `useCreateAnnotationStore`; without it there are none), annotationList (the three options `editable`, `linkEndpoints`, `isContinuousPlay`; no `annotations`), effects, trackEffects, onReady (once per mount, the first time an engine is attached and no source is pending), onError (the engine or adapter could not be built, or onReady threw; not for a failed source, not for a refused track), soundFontCache, indefinitePlayback (the animation loop and seekTo follow it), sampleRate, createAdapter. Removed: tracks, onTracksChange, deferEngineRebuild (without an `arrangement` the provider throws an Error that says so); onAnnotationsChange (the store is the one owner of the annotations). An engine is built on mount, when `effects` changes identity and when `zoomLevels` changes content, never for a track change; inline onReady/onError build nothing. Row height and bar style are NOT provider props: see `WaveformViewOptions`
- `MediaElementPlaylistProvider` — Single-track provider (HTMLAudioElement). Multiple instances per page OK (independent audio elements). Props: track, samplesPerPixel (followed, no finer than the waveform data; a zoom keeps the time under a pointer hovering over the timeline, else a selected range on screen that does not fill the view, else the cursor on screen, else the centre), playbackRate, preservesPitch, automaticScroll, theme (merged over `defaultTheme`), annotationStore, annotationList (the three options; `onAnnotationsChange` is removed), audioContext, onReady, onError, createPlayout. Row height and bar style are NOT provider props: see `WaveformViewOptions`. Track config supports fadeIn/fadeOut (requires audioContext). Use for language learning, podcasts, single-track viewers, and Tone.js effect bridging.
- `WaveformViewOptions` — The options that only affect how a view draws, for every root below it, under either provider. Props: waveHeight (px of one channel, default 80 under both providers), barWidth (default 1), barGap (default 0), roundedBars (default false), progressBarWidth (playhead line, default barWidth + barGap), fillViewport (default false; `WaveformRoot` only, `MediaElementWaveformRoot` ignores it), children. It may sit above the provider and above several providers (`<WaveformViewOptions waveHeight={100}><MediaElementPlaylistProvider …/><MediaElementPlaylistProvider …/></WaveformViewOptions>`). A prop left out is inherited from the `<WaveformViewOptions>` above, then from the defaults (0 and false are values). The roots, the parts, `Waveform`, `WaveformEditor`, `MediaElementWaveform` and the providers take none of these. It goes above a root: written among a root's children it does nothing for that root and warns once in development. A nested one cannot return an option to its default (a prop left out inherits): write the value. Corrected, each with one development warning: a waveHeight or barWidth not above 0 is replaced by the default, a barGap that is NaN by 0, a barGap that makes barWidth + barGap less than 1 is raised to `1 - barWidth`, and a progressBarWidth not above 0 is replaced by barWidth + barGap (leave `<WaveformPlayhead>` out to draw no playhead). Two roots under one provider share zoom, selection and playback and may differ in view options; automatic scroll moves only the root mounted last and a spectrogram track is drawn in only one of them (issue #803). Another zoom level: under MediaElementPlaylistProvider another provider (each is independent); under WaveformPlaylistProvider with the default Tone.js engine not available by adding a provider (single instance per page; issue #805). Migration from the provider props: https://naomiaro.github.io/waveform-playlist/docs/react/upgrading
- `Waveform` — The multitrack view, ready-made: timescale, loop region, track controls (a 200 px column), tracks, annotation boxes, selection, playhead, and the annotation text list when there are annotations. Props: className only. Nothing about what is drawn is a prop, and neither are the options of the annotation boxes and the annotation list: compose the parts for that.
- `WaveformEditor` — `Waveform` with clip headers and fade curves (inside a `ClipInteractionProvider` the header is the drag handle and the trim handles come with it). Same props.
- `MediaElementWaveform` — The MediaElement view, ready-made: timescale, the one track, annotation boxes, selection, playhead, annotation list. Props: className only. Whether annotations can be edited and link endpoints are provider options (`annotationList={{ editable, linkEndpoints }}`); the annotations are the provider's `annotationStore`.
- The view's parts (compose them inside a root; a part is drawn because it is rendered): roots `WaveformRoot` (WaveformPlaylistProvider) and `MediaElementWaveformRoot` (MediaElementPlaylistProvider), props className + children. Parts: `WaveformTimescale` (renderTick; height in px of the timescale strip, default 30), `WaveformLoopRegion`, `WaveformTrackControls` (width in px, default 200; children: the control panel of ONE track, rendered once per track; default `<DefaultTrackControls />`), `WaveformTracks` (gainScaled: draw each clip's waveform scaled by its gain; web-component equivalent: `<daw-editor gain-scaled-waveforms>`) with the children `WaveformClipHeaders`, `WaveformFades`, `WaveformRecordingPreview` (recordingState), `WaveformAnnotationBoxes` (getLabel: `(annotation, index) => string`, default the annotation's id; height in px, default 30; either provider; it wires the drag of its edges itself with its own `DragDropProvider`, enabled by the provider's `editable` option), `WaveformSelection`, `WaveformPlayhead` (renderPlayhead). `WaveformLoopRegion`, `WaveformTrackControls` and `WaveformRecordingPreview` need WaveformPlaylistProvider. A part must be a child of its root (a fragment is fine), not wrapped in another component; development builds warn in the console when it is not. A child of a root that is not a part is drawn in the scrolling tracks area. The time ruler and the controls column are not provider props: render `<WaveformTimescale />` / `<WaveformTrackControls />`. Guide: https://naomiaro.github.io/waveform-playlist/docs/react/guides/composing-the-view
- `AnnotationList` — The annotation text list, anywhere under either provider (not a part of a root). Props: height (px; without it at most 200), actions (`AnnotationAction[]`: buttons on each row while `editable` is on; an action gets the annotation, its index, the annotations and the provider's `{ linkEndpoints, continuousPlay }`), scrollActivePosition ('center' default, 'start', 'end', 'nearest', or 'none' for a list that does not follow playback), scrollActiveContainer ('nearest' default, 'all'), and a function child that draws a row (`{ annotation, index, isActive, onClick, formatTime }`). A click on a row plays the annotation, as a click on its box does. Draws nothing without annotations; without `AnnotationProvider` it draws nothing and warns once in development. Text, id and action edits are written to the provider's annotation store, each to its annotation found by id; the id field refuses an empty or duplicate id; an action gets copies of the store's list, so it may change them in place. Guide: https://naomiaro.github.io/waveform-playlist/docs/react/guides/annotations
- Track control pieces (children of `<WaveformTrackControls>`, each bound to the track it is drawn for, no track prop): `DefaultTrackControls` (name, menu, mute, solo, volume, pan; its children are drawn inside the panel below the pan slider), `TrackName`, `TrackMuteButton`, `TrackSoloButton`, `TrackVolumeSlider`, `TrackPanSlider`, `TrackMenuButton` (nothing without SpectrogramProvider or for a MIDI track), `TrackRemoveButton` (`onRemove(trackId)`; top left of the track's slot), `TrackReorderGrip` (drag grip + move up/down buttons at the right edge; the drag requires ClipInteractionProvider, the buttons work regardless). A panel of your own calls `useTrack()`; a drag grip of your own calls `useTrackReorderHandle()` (`{ handleRef, isDragSource }`). A click anywhere in a track's slot selects the track. Keep props of the children stable (an inline function renders every panel on each render of your component). `renderTrackControls`, `onRemoveTrack`, `trackReordering` and `SortableTrackControls` are removed. Example: `<WaveformTrackControls><DefaultTrackControls /><TrackRemoveButton onRemove={removeTrack} /><TrackReorderGrip /></WaveformTrackControls>`. Guide: https://naomiaro.github.io/waveform-playlist/docs/react/guides/track-management
- `ClipInteractionProvider` — Declarative wrapper for clip drag/move/trim/snap/collision. Props: snap (boolean, auto-detects beats vs timescale from BeatsAndBarsProvider context), touchOptimized (touch-delay sensors and 24px clip trim handles; left out, inherited from a provider or ClipInteractionOptions above). Every clip below it can be dragged and trimmed; `Waveform` has no `interactiveClips` or `touchOptimized` prop. Replaces manual DragDropProvider + useClipDragHandlers + modifier setup. `useClipInteractionEnabled()` hook returns true when clips at that point can be dragged and trimmed.
- `ClipInteractionOptions` — The one source of the two clip interaction options, read by every clip below. Props: enabled, touchOptimized (each inherited when left out). `ClipInteractionProvider` renders it; use it directly with your own `DragDropProvider` (`<ClipInteractionOptions enabled>` replaces the removed `<Waveform interactiveClips>`), or nested to change one option for part of the tree.
- `KeyboardShortcuts` — Self-closing component for declarative keyboard shortcut setup. Props: `playback`, `clipSplitting`, `annotations`, `undo`, `additionalShortcuts`. All booleans default to false. Must be inside WaveformPlaylistProvider.
- Buttons (from `@waveform-playlist/browser`): PlayButton, PauseButton, StopButton, RewindButton, FastForwardButton, LoopButton, SetLoopRegionButton, ClearAllButton, ZoomInButton, ZoomOutButton
- Buttons (from `@waveform-playlist/browser/tone`): ExportWavButton
- Controls (from `@waveform-playlist/browser`): MasterVolumeControl, TimeFormatSelect, AudioPosition, SelectionTimeInputs, AutomaticScrollCheckbox
- Annotation controls (from `@waveform-playlist/annotations`): ContinuousPlayCheckbox, LinkEndpointsCheckbox, EditableCheckbox, DownloadAnnotationsButton
- One owner per exported name: `@waveform-playlist/browser` re-exports nothing from other packages. `ClipTrack`, `AudioClip`, `Fade`, `AnnotationData` and `KeyboardShortcut` come from `@waveform-playlist/core` (a dependency of browser; list it in your own package.json, a strict package manager such as pnpm requires that); `TimeFormat` from `@waveform-playlist/ui-components`; `EffectsFunction` / `TrackEffectsFunction` from `@waveform-playlist/playout`. `getShortcutLabel` is removed (it is in neither browser nor core): build a shortcut's label from its fields (`key`, `metaKey`, `ctrlKey`, `altKey`, `shiftKey`) with your own strings.
